items.followUp: Define any five branches of chemistry other than those listed here.

rubric.why: Physical chemistry concerns physical properties of matter and energy changes in chemical processes.
rubric.description: Defines physical chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of physical chemistry.

rubric.why: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds.
rubric.description: Defines organic chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of organic chemistry.

rubric.why: Inorganic chemistry studies elements and their compounds, generally excluding most carbon compounds.
rubric.description: Defines inorganic chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of inorganic chemistry.

rubric.why: Biochemistry studies chemical substances or processes in living organisms.
rubric.description: Defines biochemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of biochemistry.

rubric.why: Industrial chemistry concerns the manufacture of chemicals and products on an industrial scale.
rubric.description: Defines industrial chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of industrial chemistry.

modelAnswer: Physical chemistry deals with the physical properties of matter and the energy changes involved in chemical reactions.
Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that studies carbon compounds.
Inorganic chemistry deals with the properties and reactions of elements and their compounds, generally excluding most carbon compounds.
Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and processes that occur in living organisms.
Industrial chemistry deals with the manufacture of chemical substances and products on an industrial scale.

items.followUp: Describe Rutherford’s gold-foil experiment and draw a labelled diagram of its arrangement.

rubric.why: The experiment used a discharge tube containing gas at very low pressure.
rubric.description: Describes the discharge tube and low-pressure gas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the tube and the low-pressure conditions.

rubric.why: A high potential difference was applied between the cathode and anode.
rubric.description: Identifies the electrodes and applied voltage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct electrodes and high voltage.

rubric.why: The rays originate at the cathode and move towards the anode.
rubric.description: States the direction of travel of the cathode rays.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction.

rubric.why: A fluorescent glow was observed where the rays struck the glass wall or screen.
rubric.description: Gives the observation that revealed the rays.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the fluorescent glow caused by the rays.

rubric.why: A labelled diagram should show the electrodes, the direction of the rays, and where they produce a glow.
rubric.description: Provides a labelled schematic of the apparatus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a diagram or labelled schematic showing cathode, anode, cathode-ray direction, and fluorescent screen or glass glow.

modelAnswer: Cathode rays were discovered using a glass discharge tube containing gas at very low pressure, with a cathode and an anode connected to a high-voltage source.
The rays originated at the cathode and travelled towards the anode.
A fluorescent glow appeared on the glass wall or screen where the rays struck, showing that rays travelled through the tube.

Labelled schematic: Draw an elongated glass tube and label it “gas at very low pressure”. Place the cathode (−) at the left end and the anode (+) to its right. Draw an arrow from the cathode towards the anode and label it “cathode rays”. Show and label a fluorescent screen or the glass wall where the rays strike as “fluorescent glow”. Connect the two electrodes to a high-voltage source.

items.followUp: Explain why sweating cools the body and state two factors that affect the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: The more energetic molecules escape from the liquid surface during evaporation.
rubric.description: Explains which molecules escape during evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the more energetic molecules escape.

rubric.why: The remaining liquid loses average kinetic energy, or evaporation takes heat from the surroundings, causing cooling.
rubric.description: Explains why evaporation causes cooling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking loss of energy or heat absorption to cooling.

rubric.why: Temperature, surface area, wind speed, and humidity affect the rate of evaporation.
rubric.description: Gives one factor affecting evaporation and its effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid factor and the correct effect on the rate.

rubric.why: A second distinct factor also affects the rate of evaporation.
rubric.description: Gives a second factor affecting evaporation and its effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different valid factor and the correct effect on the rate.

modelAnswer: During evaporation, the more energetic molecules escape from the surface of the liquid.
The molecules left behind have lower average kinetic energy, so the liquid cools; evaporation also takes heat from its surroundings.
A higher temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
A larger surface area increases the rate of evaporation.

items.followUp: Calculate the formula mass of CaCO₃. Use Ca = 40 u, C = 12 u, and O = 16 u.

rubric.why: The formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses, each multiplied by its subscript.
rubric.description: Sets up the formula-mass calculation correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct calculation using Na = 23 u, S = 32 u, and O = 16 u.

rubric.why: The sum of the atomic masses is 142 u.
rubric.description: Gives the formula mass with a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: Na = 23 u, S = 32 u, O = 16 u.
Formula: Formula mass of Na₂SO₄ = 2(Na) + 1(S) + 4(O).
Substitution: Formula mass = 2(23 u) + 32 u + 4(16 u).
Formula mass of Na₂SO₄ = 142 u.
